name: Frightened
summary: When a creature is frightened, any ability roll they make against the source of their fear takes a bane. If that source is a creature, their ability rolls made against the frightened creature gain an edge. A frightened creature can't willingly move closer to the source of their fear if they know the location of that source. If a creature gains the frightened condition from one source while already frightened by a different source, the new condition replaces the old one.
description: When a creature is frightened, any ability roll they make against the source of their fear takes a bane. If that source is a creature, their ability rolls made against the frightened creature gain an edge. A frightened creature can't willingly move closer to the source of their fear if they know the location of that source. If a creature gains the frightened condition from one source while already frightened by a different source, the new condition replaces the old one.
source: Draw Steel Heroes Book, ch. 5 (mcdm.heroes.v1), via Steel Compendium

name: Dazed
summary: A creature who is dazed can do only one thing on their turn: use a main action, use a maneuver, or use a move action. A dazed creature also can't use triggered actions, free triggered actions, or free maneuvers.
description: A creature who is dazed can do only one thing on their turn: use a main action, use a maneuver, or use a move action. A dazed creature also can't use triggered actions, free triggered actions, or free maneuvers.
source: Draw Steel Heroes Book, ch. 5 (mcdm.heroes.v1), via Steel Compendium

name: Slowed
summary: A creature who is slowed has speed 2 unless their speed is already lower, and they can't shift.
description: A creature who is slowed has speed 2 unless their speed is already lower, and they can't shift.
source: Draw Steel Heroes Book, ch. 5 (mcdm.heroes.v1), via Steel Compendium

name: Restrained
summary: A creature who is restrained has speed 0, can't use the Stand Up maneuver, and can't be force moved. A restrained creature takes a bane on ability rolls and on Might and Agility tests, and abilities used against them gain an edge.
description:
A creature who is restrained has speed 0, can't use the Stand Up maneuver, and can't be force moved. A restrained creature takes a bane on ability rolls and on Might and Agility tests, and abilities used against them gain an edge.

If a creature teleports while restrained, that condition ends.
source: Draw Steel Heroes Book, ch. 5 (mcdm.heroes.v1), via Steel Compendium

name: Weakened
summary: A creature who is weakened takes a bane on power rolls.
description: A creature who is weakened takes a bane on power rolls.
source: Draw Steel Heroes Book, ch. 5 (mcdm.heroes.v1), via Steel Compendium

name: Bleeding
summary: While a creature is bleeding, whenever they use a main action, use a triggered action, or make a test or ability roll using Might or Agility, they lose Stamina equal to 1d6 + their level after the main action, triggered action, or power roll is resolved. This Stamina loss can't be prevented in any way, and only happens once per action.
description:
While a creature is bleeding, whenever they use a main action, use a triggered action, or make a test or ability roll using Might or Agility, they lose Stamina equal to 1d6 + their level after the main action, triggered action, or power roll is resolved. This Stamina loss can't be prevented in any way, and only happens once per action.

You take damage from this condition when you use a main action off your turn. For example, a signature ability used as a free triggered action with the assistance of the tactician's Strike Now ability triggers the damage from the bleeding condition.
source: Draw Steel Heroes Book, ch. 5 (mcdm.heroes.v1), via Steel Compendium

name: Burning
summary: Burning is not one of Draw Steel's nine conditions and has no rule of its own. Each ability that sets a creature burning says what the fire does and how it ends, so read the ability that caused it.
description: Burning is not one of Draw Steel's nine conditions and has no rule of its own. Each ability that sets a creature burning says what the fire does and how it ends, so read the ability that caused it.
source: custom

name: Taunted
summary: A creature who is taunted has a double bane on ability rolls for any ability that doesn't target the creature who taunted them, as long as they have line of effect to that creature. If a creature gains the taunted condition from one source while already taunted by a different source, the new condition replaces the old one.
description: A creature who is taunted has a double bane on ability rolls for any ability that doesn't target the creature who taunted them, as long as they have line of effect to that creature. If a creature gains the taunted condition from one source while already taunted by a different source, the new condition replaces the old one.
source: Draw Steel Heroes Book, ch. 5 (mcdm.heroes.v1), via Steel Compendium

name: Prone
summary: While a creature is prone, they are flat on the ground, any strike they make takes a bane, and melee abilities used against them gain an edge. A prone creature must crawl to move along the ground, which costs 1 additional square of movement for every square crawled. A creature can't climb, jump, swim, or fly while prone. If they are climbing, flying, or jumping when knocked prone, they fall.
description:
While a creature is prone, they are flat on the ground, any strike they make takes a bane, and melee abilities used against them gain an edge. A prone creature must crawl to move along the ground, which costs 1 additional square of movement for every square crawled. A creature can't climb, jump, swim, or fly while prone. If they are climbing, flying, or jumping when knocked prone, they fall.

Unless the ability or effect that imposed the prone condition says otherwise, a prone creature can stand up using the Stand Up maneuver. A creature adjacent to a willing prone creature can likewise use the Stand Up maneuver to make that creature stand up.
source: Draw Steel Heroes Book, ch. 5 (mcdm.heroes.v1), via Steel Compendium

name: Charmed
summary: Charmed is not one of Draw Steel's nine conditions and has no rule of its own. Each ability that charms a creature says what the charm does and how it ends, so read the ability that caused it.
description: Charmed is not one of Draw Steel's nine conditions and has no rule of its own. Each ability that charms a creature says what the charm does and how it ends, so read the ability that caused it.
source: custom

name: Grabbed
summary: A creature who is grabbed has speed 0, can't be force moved except by a creature, object, or effect that has them grabbed, can't use the Knockback maneuver, and takes a bane on abilities that don't target the creature, object, or effect that has them grabbed. If a creature is grabbed by another creature and that creature moves, they bring the grabbed creature with them. If a creature's size is equal to or less than the size of a creature they have grabbed, their speed is halved while they have that creature grabbed.
description:
A creature who is grabbed has speed 0, can't be force moved except by a creature, object, or effect that has them grabbed, can't use the Knockback maneuver, and takes a bane on abilities that don't target the creature, object, or effect that has them grabbed. If a creature is grabbed by another creature and that creature moves, they bring the grabbed creature with them. If a creature's size is equal to or less than the size of a creature they have grabbed, their speed is halved while they have that creature grabbed.

A creature who has another creature grabbed can use a maneuver to move the grabbed creature into an unoccupied space adjacent to them.

A creature can release a creature they have grabbed at any time to end that condition (no action required). A grabbed creature can attempt to escape being grabbed using the Escape Grab maneuver. If a grabbed creature teleports, or if either the grabbed creature or the creature grabbing them is force moved so that both creatures are not adjacent to each other, that creature is no longer grabbed.

A creature can grab only creatures of their size or smaller. If a creature's Might score is 2 or higher, they can grab any creature larger than them with a size equal to or less than their Might score.

Unless otherwise indicated, a creature can grab only one creature at a time.
source: Draw Steel Heroes Book, ch. 5 (mcdm.heroes.v1), via Steel Compendium

name: Hidden
summary: While you are hidden from another creature, the creature can't target you with abilities that don't have the Area keyword. This benefit ends as soon as you are no longer hidden from that creature.
description:
While you are hidden from another creature, the creature can't target you with abilities that don't have the Area keyword. This benefit ends as soon as you are no longer hidden from that creature.

Additionally, while you are hidden from another creature, you gain an edge on ability rolls made against that creature. This benefit lasts until the end of the turn in which you are no longer hidden.

You are no longer hidden from a creature if you don't have cover or concealment from them. If you use an ability, interact with an enemy, move without sneaking, or otherwise make noise or reveal yourself while hidden, you are no longer hidden once the activity that reveals you resolves.
source: Draw Steel Heroes Book, ch. 9 (mcdm.heroes.v1), via Steel Compendium

name: Shift
summary: A shift is a special movement that doesn't provoke opportunity attacks or free strikes. The creature moves the indicated number of squares.
description: A shift is a special movement that doesn't provoke opportunity attacks or free strikes. The creature moves the indicated number of squares.

name: Push
summary: Forced movement that moves the target the indicated number of squares away from the source. The target doesn't provoke opportunity attacks from this movement.
description: Forced movement that moves the target the indicated number of squares away from the source. The target doesn't provoke opportunity attacks from this movement.

name: Pull
summary: Forced movement that moves the target the indicated number of squares toward the source. The target doesn't provoke opportunity attacks from this movement.
description: Forced movement that moves the target the indicated number of squares toward the source. The target doesn't provoke opportunity attacks from this movement.

name: EoT
summary: End of Turn. The effect lasts until the end of the affected creature's next turn, then ends automatically.
description: End of Turn. The effect lasts until the end of the affected creature's next turn, then ends automatically.

name: Save Ends
summary: The effect persists until the affected creature succeeds on a saving throw at the end of their turn (roll a d10; 6 or higher ends the effect).
description: The effect persists until the affected creature succeeds on a saving throw at the end of their turn (roll a d10; 6 or higher ends the effect).

name: Temporary Stamina
summary: Extra stamina layered on top of current stamina.
description: Extra stamina layered on top of current stamina. Damage reduces temporary stamina first. Temporary stamina doesn't stack; use the higher value. It expires at the end of the encounter.

name: Free Strike
summary: A quick, automatic attack a creature can make outside their turn. Typically triggered by an enemy moving out of reach or as part of certain abilities.
description: A quick, automatic attack a creature can make outside their turn. Typically triggered by an enemy moving out of reach or as part of certain abilities.

name: Forced Movement
summary: Movement imposed on a creature by an outside force (push, pull, slide). Forced movement doesn't provoke opportunity attacks or free strikes.
description: Movement imposed on a creature by an outside force (push, pull, slide). Forced movement doesn't provoke opportunity attacks or free strikes.

name: Power Roll
summary: Roll 2d10 and add a characteristic. Results: 11 or lower (Tier 1), 12-16 (Tier 2), 17+ (Tier 3). An edge adds 2 and a bane subtracts 2. A natural 19 or 20 is always a Tier 3 result.
description: Roll 2d10 and add a characteristic. Results: 11 or lower (Tier 1), 12-16 (Tier 2), 17+ (Tier 3). An edge adds 2 and a bane subtracts 2. A natural 19 or 20 is always a Tier 3 result.

name: Stability
summary: Reduces forced movement. When a creature would be force-moved, reduce the distance by their stability value (minimum 0).
description: Reduces forced movement. When a creature would be force-moved, reduce the distance by their stability value (minimum 0).

name: Winded
summary: A creature is winded when their stamina drops to their winded value (half their maximum stamina) or below. Some abilities trigger or change when the creature is winded.
description: A creature is winded when their stamina drops to their winded value (half their maximum stamina) or below. Some abilities trigger or change when the creature is winded.

name: Edge
summary: An edge grants +2 to your power roll. Edges and banes never stack past two — a double edge bumps the result up a tier instead, and one edge and one bane cancel out.
description: An edge grants +2 to your power roll. Edges and banes never stack past two — a double edge bumps the result up a tier instead, and one edge and one bane cancel out.

name: Bane
summary: A bane imposes −2 on your power roll. Edges and banes never stack past two — a double bane drops the result down a tier instead, and one bane and one edge cancel out.
description: A bane imposes −2 on your power roll. Edges and banes never stack past two — a double bane drops the result down a tier instead, and one bane and one edge cancel out.

name: Magic
summary: An ability with the Magic keyword draws on magic. Some effects, creatures, and treasures interact specifically with Magic abilities.
description: An ability with the Magic keyword draws on magic. Some effects, creatures, and treasures interact specifically with Magic abilities.

name: Psionic
summary: An ability with the Psionic keyword draws on the power of the mind. Some effects interact specifically with Psionic abilities.
description: An ability with the Psionic keyword draws on the power of the mind. Some effects interact specifically with Psionic abilities.

name: Melee
summary: A Melee ability can be used against targets within reach (adjacent unless a greater melee distance is noted).
description: A Melee ability can be used against targets within reach (adjacent unless a greater melee distance is noted).

name: Ranged
summary: A Ranged ability can be used against targets at a distance, up to its listed range.
description: A Ranged ability can be used against targets at a distance, up to its listed range.

name: Weapon
summary: A Weapon ability is made with a held weapon and benefits from your kit's weapon damage bonuses.
description: A Weapon ability is made with a held weapon and benefits from your kit's weapon damage bonuses.

name: Strike
summary: A Strike ability makes one or more attacks against a target, typically dealing damage on a power roll.
description: A Strike ability makes one or more attacks against a target, typically dealing damage on a power roll.

name: Area
summary: An Area ability affects every valid target within a defined zone (a burst, cube, line, or wall).
description: An Area ability affects every valid target within a defined zone (a burst, cube, line, or wall).

name: Slide
summary: Forced movement that moves the target up to the indicated number of squares in any direction except vertically. Unlike a push or a pull, a slide doesn't have to be a straight line.
description: Forced movement that moves the target up to the indicated number of squares in any direction except vertically. Unlike a push or a pull, a slide doesn't have to be a straight line.

name: Saving Throw
summary: A roll made at the end of your turn to shake off an effect that ends with a save. Roll a d10; on a 6 or higher the effect ends, otherwise it continues.
description: A roll made at the end of your turn to shake off an effect that ends with a save. Roll a d10; on a 6 or higher the effect ends, otherwise it continues.

name: Potency
summary: An added effect lands only if its potency value is higher than the target's listed characteristic score.
description: An added effect lands only if its potency value is higher than the target's listed characteristic score. Potencies are written as a characteristic letter, a less-than sign, and a value — M < WEAK, A < AVERAGE, R < STRONG. Your weak, average, and strong potency values are your highest characteristic score minus 2, minus 1, and unmodified.

name: Surge
summary: Stored momentum. Whenever you deal rolled damage you can spend up to 3 surges against one target, each dealing extra damage equal to your highest characteristic score;…
description: Stored momentum. Whenever you deal rolled damage you can spend up to 3 surges against one target, each dealing extra damage equal to your highest characteristic score; alternatively, spend 2 surges to raise one potency by 1 for one target. Any surges left over are lost at the end of combat.

name: Recovery
summary: A second wind you can spend. Your recovery value is one-third of your Stamina maximum rounded down, and spending a Recovery regains that much Stamina. Your number of Recoveries…
description: A second wind you can spend. Your recovery value is one-third of your Stamina maximum rounded down, and spending a Recovery regains that much Stamina. Your number of Recoveries comes from your class, and finishing a respite restores all of them.

name: Respite
summary: 24 uninterrupted hours of rest plus one respite activity.
description: 24 uninterrupted hours of rest plus one respite activity. Finishing a respite restores all your Stamina and Recoveries and converts your Victories into Experience. A night's sleep is not a respite.

name: Damage Immunity
summary: Reduces damage of the stated type by the immunity's value, to a minimum of 0; an immunity of "all" ignores that damage entirely.
description: Reduces damage of the stated type by the immunity's value, to a minimum of 0; an immunity of "all" ignores that damage entirely. Immunity is applied last when calculating damage, and only the highest applicable immunity counts.

name: Damage Weakness
summary: The mirror of damage immunity — you take extra damage of the stated type equal to the weakness value.
description: The mirror of damage immunity — you take extra damage of the stated type equal to the weakness value. Weakness is applied before immunity, and only the highest applicable weakness counts.

name: Concealment
summary: Darkness, fog, invisibility, and any other effect that fully obscures a creature without protecting their physical form grants concealment.
description: Darkness, fog, invisibility, and any other effect that fully obscures a creature without protecting their physical form grants concealment. You can still target a creature who has concealment as long as they aren't hidden, but strikes against them take a bane.

name: Cover
summary: A target has cover when you have line of effect to them but at least half their form is blocked by a solid object such as a tree, a wall, or an overturned table.
description: A target has cover when you have line of effect to them but at least half their form is blocked by a solid object such as a tree, a wall, or an overturned table. Damage-dealing abilities used against a target with cover take a bane.

name: Difficult Terrain
summary: Thick underbrush, rubble, webs, and similar obstacles create difficult terrain.
description: Thick underbrush, rubble, webs, and similar obstacles create difficult terrain. It costs 1 additional square of movement to enter a square of difficult terrain. Forced movement ignores it.

name: Flanking
summary: You are flanking an enemy when you and at least one ally are adjacent to them on opposite sides.
description: You are flanking an enemy when you and at least one ally are adjacent to them on opposite sides. While flanking, you gain an edge on melee strikes against that enemy. You must have line of effect to the enemy and be able to take triggered actions to gain or grant the benefit.

name: Critical Hit
summary: An ability roll made as a main action that comes up a natural 19 or 20 — the total on the dice before adding your characteristic score or any other modifier — is a critical hit.
description: An ability roll made as a main action that comes up a natural 19 or 20 — the total on the dice before adding your characteristic score or any other modifier — is a critical hit. You immediately take an additional main action after resolving the power roll, even off your turn and even while dazed. Rolls made as maneuvers or other action types can't crit.

name: Dying
summary: You are dying while your Stamina is 0 or lower.
description: You are dying while your Stamina is 0 or lower. A dying creature is bleeding and that instance of the condition can't be removed until they stop dying, and they can't use the Catch Breath maneuver in combat. If your Stamina falls to the negative of your winded value, you die.

name: Surprised
summary: A creature who isn't ready for combat when it starts is surprised until the end of the first combat round.
description: A creature who isn't ready for combat when it starts is surprised until the end of the first combat round. A surprised creature can't take triggered actions or free triggered actions, and ability rolls made against them gain an edge.

name: Triggered Action
summary: An action you can take only when its stated trigger occurs, on your turn or another creature's. You get one triggered action per round.
description: An action you can take only when its stated trigger occurs, on your turn or another creature's. You get one triggered action per round.

name: Free Triggered Action
summary: Follows the same rules as a triggered action but doesn't count against your one-per-round limit. Anything that stops you taking triggered actions also stops free triggered actions.
description: Follows the same rules as a triggered action but doesn't count against your one-per-round limit. Anything that stops you taking triggered actions also stops free triggered actions.

name: Main Action
summary: The heaviest of the three things you get on your turn.
description: The heaviest of the three things you get on your turn. Most class, kit, and treasure abilities are main actions, as are Charge, Defend, Heal, and Free Strike. You can convert a main action into a maneuver or a move action.

name: Maneuver
summary: One of the three things you get on your turn, involving less focus and exertion than a main action.
description: One of the three things you get on your turn, involving less focus and exertion than a main action. Aid Attack, Catch Breath, Escape Grab, Grab, Hide, Knockback, Stand Up, and Use Consumable are maneuvers.

name: Move Action
summary: The part of your turn spent getting around the battlefield: Advance, Disengage, or Ride. You can break the movement up before, after, or between your maneuver and main action.
description: The part of your turn spent getting around the battlefield: Advance, Disengage, or Ride. You can break the movement up before, after, or between your maneuver and main action.

name: Disengage
summary: A move action. You shift 1 square. Certain kits, class features, and ancestry traits let you shift further when you disengage.
description: A move action. You shift 1 square. Certain kits, class features, and ancestry traits let you shift further when you disengage.

name: Catch Breath
summary: A maneuver. You spend a Recovery and regain Stamina equal to your recovery value. A dying creature can't use it in combat, though allies can still help them spend Recoveries.
description: A maneuver. You spend a Recovery and regain Stamina equal to your recovery value. A dying creature can't use it in combat, though allies can still help them spend Recoveries.

name: Echelon
summary: The four tiers of play, each covering a band of levels: 1st echelon is 1st to 3rd level, 2nd echelon is 4th to 6th level, 3rd echelon is 7th to 9th level, and 4th echelon is 10th…
description: The four tiers of play, each covering a band of levels: 1st echelon is 1st to 3rd level, 2nd echelon is 4th to 6th level, 3rd echelon is 7th to 9th level, and 4th echelon is 10th level. Bonuses that scale per echelon — such as a kit's Stamina bonus — increase as your hero crosses into each band.

name: Encounter Value
summary: Every Director-controlled creature has an encounter value (EV), the number of budget points it costs to buy that creature for a combat encounter.
description: Every Director-controlled creature has an encounter value (EV), the number of budget points it costs to buy that creature for a combat encounter. The EV printed for a minion covers four minions together, not one.

name: Encounter Strength
summary: A party's encounter strength (ES) is the benchmark the Director buys monsters against.
description: A party's encounter strength (ES) is the benchmark the Director buys monsters against. Each hero's encounter strength is 4 plus 2 for each of their levels, so a 3rd-level hero is worth 10; add every hero together for the party's ES. Retainers and other NPCs fighting alongside the heroes count as heroes of their own level.

name: Malice
summary: Malice is the Director's resource, the counterpart to a hero's Heroic Resource, spent to activate monsters' most powerful abilities.
description: Malice is the Director's resource, the counterpart to a hero's Heroic Resource, spent to activate monsters' most powerful abilities. At the start of combat the Director gains Malice equal to the average number of Victories per hero, then at the start of each combat round gains Malice equal to the number of heroes in the battle plus the round number. A hero who dies stops generating Malice, and any unused Malice is lost at the end of an encounter.

name: Montage Test
summary: A big job — sneaking in, crossing a wasteland — played as a run of smaller tests instead of one roll.
description: A montage test turns one big job that would otherwise be hand-waved — getting into a barrow unseen, crossing a hostile desert — into a run of individual tests. Each hero tackles a stretch of it their own way, with whatever skill fits the moment. The Director decides how many successes the party needs to pull it off and how many failures it can absorb; a failure is pressure, not a stop, and whichever total fills first decides how the job goes.
source: custom

name: Minion
summary: A weak solo creature that fights in a squad — the squad shares one Stamina pool and loses a minion each time it drops by that much.
description: A minion is weak on its own but dangerous in numbers. A squad of minions shares a single Stamina pool: each time damage empties one minion's worth of that pool, one minion in the squad falls, so a single big hit can carry on and drop more than one. Minions never take conditions that would only slow them down, and a minion's listed encounter value covers a small group of them, not one.
source: custom

name: Captain
summary: A stronger creature leading a squad of minions — the minions fight harder while their captain is still standing.
description: A captain is a sturdier creature placed in charge of a squad of minions. While their captain is alive and near them, the squad's minions fight noticeably harder — the exact bonus is the captain's own trait. Taking the captain down (or moving the squad out of its reach) is usually the fastest way to blunt the whole squad at once.
source: custom

name: Solo Creature
summary: A single powerful creature built to stand in for a whole encounter's worth of monsters.
description: A solo creature is built to fight an entire party by itself, in place of a room full of smaller monsters. It has a large Stamina pool, extra actions each round, and its own Malice-fuelled abilities, so a fight against one plays very differently from a fight against a crowd — the party is spending its resources against one relentless threat instead of thinning a group.
source: custom

name: Victories
summary: A running tally of the fights a party has come through — spent on a respite for lasting rewards.
description: Victories are a running tally of the notable fights and challenges a party has come through. They build up across a session and are spent when the party takes a respite, where they convert into Experience Points the party can use for lasting rewards between adventures. They aren't a resource spent mid-combat.
source: custom

name: Big Versus Little
summary: When a larger creature force moves a smaller target with a melee weapon ability, the distance of the forced movement is increased by 1. If a smaller creature force moves a larger target with a melee weapon ability, the distance doesn't change.
description: When a larger creature force moves a smaller target with a melee weapon ability, the distance of the forced movement is increased by 1. If a smaller creature force moves a larger target with a melee weapon ability, the distance doesn't change.
source: Draw Steel Heroes Book, ch. 10 (mcdm.heroes.v1), via Steel Compendium

name: Burrow
summary: A creature who has "burrow" in their speed entry, or who gains the temporary ability to burrow, can move through dirt horizontally, and either has the means to breathe while doing so or doesn't require air to live. Such creatures can't move through more solid ground, such as stone, unless their stat block or the effect that lets them burrow says otherwise. Similarly, a burrowing creature doesn't leave a tunnel unless the rules say so.
description: A creature who has "burrow" in their speed entry, or who gains the temporary ability to burrow, can move through dirt horizontally, and either has the means to breathe while doing so or doesn't require air to live. Such creatures can't move through more solid ground, such as stone, unless their stat block or the effect that lets them burrow says otherwise. Similarly, a burrowing creature doesn't leave a tunnel unless the rules say so.
source: Draw Steel Heroes Book, ch. 10 (mcdm.heroes.v1), via Steel Compendium

name: Burrowing Forced Movement
summary: While a creature who is completely beneath the ground while burrowing is force moved by movement that isn't vertical, they aren't moved, and they take 1 damage for each square they would have been force moved. If the forced movement is vertical, the creature is moved through the dirt as if it were air.
description: While a creature who is completely beneath the ground while burrowing is force moved by movement that isn't vertical, they aren't moved, and they take 1 damage for each square they would have been force moved. If the forced movement is vertical, the creature is moved through the dirt as if it were air.
source: Draw Steel Heroes Book, ch. 10 (mcdm.heroes.v1), via Steel Compendium

name: Climb or Swim
summary: A creature who has "climb" in their speed entry, or who gains the temporary ability to automatically climb, can climb across vertical and horizontal surfaces at full speed. Likewise, a creature who has "swim" in their speed entry, or who gains the temporary ability to automatically swim, can swim in liquid at full speed.
description:
A creature who has "climb" in their speed entry, or who gains the temporary ability to automatically climb, can climb across vertical and horizontal surfaces at full speed. Likewise, a creature who has "swim" in their speed entry, or who gains the temporary ability to automatically swim, can swim in liquid at full speed.

Creatures without those types of movement can still climb or swim when a rule allows them to move, but each square of climbing or swimming costs 2 squares of movement. If a surface is difficult to climb (for instance, a sheer cliff or ice-covered wall) or a liquid is hard to swim through (a raging river or whirlpool), the Director can call for a Might test. On a failure, a creature can't climb or swim but wastes no movement in the attempt. The Director can also impose other consequences to failure, such as being caught in the spinning current of a whirlpool.
source: Draw Steel Heroes Book, ch. 10 (mcdm.heroes.v1), via Steel Compendium

name: Climbing Other Creatures
summary: You can attempt to climb a creature whose size is greater than yours. If the creature is willing, you can climb them without any trouble. If the creature is unwilling, you make the following test:
description:
You can attempt to climb a creature whose size is greater than yours. If the creature is willing, you can climb them without any trouble. If the creature is unwilling, you make the following test:

Power Roll + Might or Agility:

- ≤11: You fail to climb the creature, and they can make a free strike against you.
- 12-16: You fail to climb the creature.
- 17+: You climb the creature.

While you climb or ride a creature, you gain an edge on melee abilities used against them. The creature can use a maneuver to attempt to knock you off, forcing you to make the following test:

Power Roll + Might or Agility:

- ≤11: You fall off the creature into an unoccupied adjacent space of your choice, taking falling damage and landing prone as usual.
- 12-16: You slide down the creature into an unoccupied adjacent space of your choice and don't land prone.
- 17+: You continue to hold on to the creature.

If you are knocked prone while climbing or riding a creature, you fall and land prone in an adjacent space of your choice, taking damage as usual from the fall.
source: Draw Steel Heroes Book, ch. 10 (mcdm.heroes.v1), via Steel Compendium

name: Crawl
summary: If you are prone, you can remain prone and crawl on the ground. Doing so costs you 1 additional square of movement for every square you crawl. If you intentionally want to crawl, you can fall prone as a free maneuver. While voluntarily prone, you can choose to stand as a free maneuver.

name: Death Effects and Forced Movement
summary: Some creatures have traits or abilities that trigger when they die or are reduced to 0 Stamina. If such a creature is reduced to 0 Stamina by damage from an ability or effect that also force moves them, the forced movement takes place before the triggered effect.

name: Dig Maneuver
summary: It takes extra effort to dig vertically through the ground as opposed to tunneling horizontally, requiring a creature to use a special maneuver. To use the Dig maneuver, a creature must have "burrow" in their speed entry, they must have a speed that is equal to or greater than their size, and they must be touching terrain that can be burrowed through.
description:
It takes extra effort to dig vertically through the ground as opposed to tunneling horizontally, requiring a creature to use a special maneuver. To use the Dig maneuver, a creature must have "burrow" in their speed entry, they must have a speed that is equal to or greater than their size, and they must be touching terrain that can be burrowed through.

When a creature uses the Dig maneuver, they can move vertically up to a number of squares equal to their size. If a burrowing creature has a creature who is not unconscious grabbed, they can't willingly move deeper into the ground. It's too difficult to dig with a flailing enemy in your claws.
source: Draw Steel Heroes Book, ch. 10 (mcdm.heroes.v1), via Steel Compendium

name: Falling Far
summary: When a creature first falls from a great height, they fall 100 squares in the first round. At the end of each subsequent round that they remain falling, they fall another 100 squares.

name: Falling Onto Another Creature
summary: A creature who falls and lands on another creature causes that creature to take the same damage from the fall. The falling creature then lands prone in the nearest unoccupied space of their choice. If the falling creature's size is greater than the Might score of the creature they land on, that creature is knocked prone.

name: Fly
summary: A creature who has "fly" in their speed entry, or who gains the temporary ability to fly, can move through the air vertically or horizontally at full speed and remain in midair. If a flying creature is knocked prone or has their speed reduced to 0, they fall.

name: Forced Into a Fall
summary: If you can't fly and are force moved across an open space that would cause you to fall, such as being pushed over the edge of a cliff, you continue moving the total distance you were moved first. If you are still in a position to fall when the forced movement ends, you fall.

summary: A creature who has "hover" in their speed entry (most commonly alongside "fly" or "teleport"), or who gains the temporary ability to hover, can remain motionless in midair. They don't fall even if they are knocked prone or their speed is reduced to 0.

name: Hurling Through Objects
summary: When you move a creature into a mundane object, the object can break depending on how many squares of forced movement remain. The cost of being slammed into an object is tied to the damage a target takes for being hurled through it:
description:
When you move a creature into a mundane object, the object can break depending on how many squares of forced movement remain. The cost of being slammed into an object is tied to the damage a target takes for being hurled through it:

- It costs 1 remaining square of forced movement to destroy 1 square of glass. The creature moved takes 3 damage.
- It costs 3 remaining squares of forced movement to destroy 1 square of wood. The creature moved takes 5 damage.
- It costs 6 remaining squares of forced movement to destroy 1 square of stone. The creature moved takes 8 damage.
- It costs 9 remaining squares of forced movement to destroy 1 square of metal. The creature moved takes 11 damage.

If any forced movement remains after the object is destroyed, you can continue to move the creature who destroyed the object.
source: Draw Steel Heroes Book, ch. 10 (mcdm.heroes.v1), via Steel Compendium

name: Jump
summary: Whenever an effect allows you to move (including using the Advance move action), you can automatically long jump a number of squares up to your Might or Agility score (your choice; minimum 1 square) as part of that movement. The height of your jump is automatically 1 square as part of that movement.
description:
Whenever an effect allows you to move (including using the Advance move action), you can automatically long jump a number of squares up to your Might or Agility score (your choice; minimum 1 square) as part of that movement. The height of your jump is automatically 1 square as part of that movement.

If you want to jump even longer or higher than your baseline jump allows, make a Might or Agility test:

Power Roll + Might or Agility:

- ≤11: You don't jump any farther than your baseline jump allows.
- 12-16: You jump 1 square longer and higher than your baseline jump allows.
- 17+: You jump 2 squares longer and higher than your baseline jump allows.

You can't jump farther or higher than the distance of the effect that allows you to move. You can't jump out of difficult terrain or damaging terrain.
source: Draw Steel Heroes Book, ch. 10 (mcdm.heroes.v1), via Steel Compendium

name: Non-Burrowing Creatures
summary: If you are on the ground and adjacent to a creature who is beneath the ground while burrowing, you can use a maneuver to pull that creature up 1 square out of the ground, provided the creature is willing.
description:
If you are on the ground and adjacent to a creature who is beneath the ground while burrowing, you can use a maneuver to pull that creature up 1 square out of the ground, provided the creature is willing.

If a creature who can't burrow wants to dig into the ground, they can use the following ability provided their speed is 2 or more.

Claw Dirt

Maneuver
Self · Self

Power Roll + Might:

- ≤11: You can move 1 square into, out of, or through ground you are touching that can be burrowed through, and you are slowed and weakened (EoT).
- 12-16: You can use your main action this turn to move 1 square into, out of, or through ground you are touching that can be burrowed through, and you are slowed (EoT).
- 17+: You can move 1 square into, out of, or through ground you are touching that can be burrowed through.
source: Draw Steel Heroes Book, ch. 10 (mcdm.heroes.v1), via Steel Compendium

name: Slamming Into Objects
summary: When a creature force moves a target into a stationary object that is the target's size or larger and the object doesn't break, the movement ends and the target takes 2 damage plus 1 damage for each square remaining in their forced movement.
description:
When a creature force moves a target into a stationary object that is the target's size or larger and the object doesn't break, the movement ends and the target takes 2 damage plus 1 damage for each square remaining in their forced movement.

If you force move a creature downward into an object that doesn't break (including the ground), they also take falling damage as if they had fallen the distance force moved and their Agility score was 0.

Tracking Object Forced-Movement Damage

At the Director's discretion, mundane objects that are force moved into creatures or other objects take damage as if they were creatures. Sturdy objects can take damage as follows before they are destroyed:

- Wood object: 3 damage for each square it occupies
- Stone object: 6 damage for each square it occupies
- Metal object: 9 damage for each square it occupies

More fragile objects are destroyed after taking any damage.
source: Draw Steel Heroes Book, ch. 10 (mcdm.heroes.v1), via Steel Compendium

name: Slamming into Creatures
summary: When you force move a creature into another creature, the movement ends and both creatures take 1 damage for each square remaining in the first creature's forced movement. You can also force move an object into a creature. The object's movement ends, and the creature takes 1 damage for each square remaining in the object's forced movement.
description:
When you force move a creature into another creature, the movement ends and both creatures take 1 damage for each square remaining in the first creature's forced movement. You can also force move an object into a creature. The object's movement ends, and the creature takes 1 damage for each square remaining in the object's forced movement.

It's possible to move a creature or object of a larger size into several creatures of a smaller size at the same time. When this happens, the larger creature in the collision takes damage only once, not once for each smaller creature they slam into.

If a creature is killed by damage from an ability or effect that also force moves them, a second creature they are slammed into still takes damage unless the Director deems otherwise.

You can force move another creature into yourself with a pull or a slide.
source: Draw Steel Heroes Book, ch. 10 (mcdm.heroes.v1), via Steel Compendium

name: Targeting Burrowing Creatures
summary: If you are on the ground, you have line of effect to a burrowing creature if that creature occupies 1 or more squares of terrain that can be burrowed through and that touch the ground, and if you have line of effect to any of those squares. The burrowing creature gains the benefit of cover from you.
description:
If you are on the ground, you have line of effect to a burrowing creature if that creature occupies 1 or more squares of terrain that can be burrowed through and that touch the ground, and if you have line of effect to any of those squares. The burrowing creature gains the benefit of cover from you.

If you are completely beneath the ground while burrowing, you don't have line of effect to any creature on the surface unless a rule states otherwise.

If you are completely beneath the ground while burrowing and are adjacent to another creature who is burrowing, you have line of effect to that creature, though you both have cover from each other.

You can't gain the benefit of high ground against creatures who are completely beneath the ground while burrowing.
source: Draw Steel Heroes Book, ch. 10 (mcdm.heroes.v1), via Steel Compendium

name: Teleport
summary: When a creature teleports, they move from one space to another space instantaneously. The following rules apply to teleporting:
description:
When a creature teleports, they move from one space to another space instantaneously. The following rules apply to teleporting:

- Teleporting doesn't provoke opportunity attacks or other effects that are triggered by a creature moving.
- When a creature teleports, they bypass any obstacles between the space they leave and their destination space.
- A creature teleporting themself must have line of effect to their destination space. A creature teleporting another creature must have line of effect from the space the teleported creature leaves and to their destination space.
- A teleporting creature's destination space can't be occupied by another creature or object.
- The effect that lets a creature teleport indicates how far they can teleport. That distance can be greater than the creature's speed.
- If a creature can teleport as part of their usual movement, they can use the Advance move action to teleport a number of squares up to their usual speed, unmodified by conditions or effects.
- If a creature teleports while prone, they can be standing when they reach their destination space provided they are able to stand. If a prone creature is teleported by another creature, it is up to that creature whether the teleported creature remains prone or stands if they are able.
- If you teleport while affected by the grabbed or restrained conditions, those conditions end for you.
- When a creature teleports, they must leave the space where they start and enter a new space. A creature can't teleport to and from the same space.
source: Draw Steel Heroes Book, ch. 10 (mcdm.heroes.v1), via Steel Compendium

name: Vertical
summary: If a forced movement effect has the word "vertical" in front of it, then the forced movement can move a target up or down in addition to horizontally. For example, if a forced movement effect says "vertical push 5," then a creature targeted by the effect can be pushed up to 5 squares in any direction, as long as the forced movement is a straight line.
description:
If a forced movement effect has the word "vertical" in front of it, then the forced movement can move a target up or down in addition to horizontally. For example, if a forced movement effect says "vertical push 5," then a creature targeted by the effect can be pushed up to 5 squares in any direction, as long as the forced movement is a straight line.

If a creature who can't fly is left in midair at the end of a vertical forced move, they fall. Forced movement made against a creature who is flying is always a vertical forced move, whether or not the effect specifies it.

Though you can't freely push, pull, or slide a target up and down unless that forced movement specifies "vertical," you can move them along a physical slope such as a hill or staircase. For a target to be force moved along a slope, each square of the slope can be no more than 1 square higher or lower than the previous square.
source: Draw Steel Heroes Book, ch. 10 (mcdm.heroes.v1), via Steel Compendium
